questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to an English speaking country with beautiful landscape. Cork was the perfect choice because it is a very student-friendly city with plenty to do and not too big city for a 4 months stay. I also read good reviews on Mobility.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay. There is a lot of paper work, and it can be a bit annoying sometimes as it differs from student to student depending on the destination or field of study. But it’s totally worth it!!!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Orientation the first days and there is an international office where you can go if you have any questions. I didn't need assistance but I heard they are very nice and helpful if you have issues with overlapping courses and stuff.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Ireland is experiencing a BIG house crisis, so you need to start early if you want to find an affordable place. I read about a place called Brookfield Village on Mobility, which is probably the cheapest option. I lived with 7 others students, it was a bit old but it worked out fine for 4 months.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Get use to walk a lot in Cork in general, you can't rely on the buses... But you don’t want to live farther than 30-40min walking distance from the center.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They have a an entire course catalog for visiting students, which is easy to find. However I needed to take 6 classes, and it was difficult to make it fit into the timetable.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Again, the international office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was refused one class, which wasn’t the most important for me, but the frustrating part was finding another class that fit into the timetable and then waiting 2 more weeks for a final response.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Just be patient, even if it can be a bit stressfull, I didn’t hear anyone for whom it didn’t work out for in the end. When choosing classes, the ones starting with 1 are first-year, 2 second-year and so on. 
It might also be a good idea to check the exam format, so you don’t end up with only final exams.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was a little lower than UCPH, same for the exams, but the challenge for me was to manage having 6 courses at the same time, and some with hand written final exams.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The professors are very nice and engaged, but the students don’t really participate.
The classes were mostly lectures, with few or no practice classes like we’re used to at UCPH. Instead they have more continuous assignments

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: BL3004: Key Research Skills in Biology, MB3005: The role and ecology of microbes in the environment, MB3012: Transmission and Epidemiology of Infectious Diseases, MB3022: Virology, ZY3019: Adaptations to Extreme Environments, HI115: Introduction to Modern Irish History for visiting students

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Key Research Skills in Biology and Adaptations to Extreme Environments were 2 courses I read about in Mobility from previous students and I liked them as well. The first course was helpful for academic writing and work with R again, while Adaptations was really interesting with great guest professors. At the end I had to write a paper, which is great practice for the bachelor thesis.
The microbiology (MB) courses were fine, it was nice having 3 courses with the same group of students. I was expecting more of the history course, but I liked trying something different and less demanding.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I ended up spending more money than I expected:) Trips, going out, and basically leaving like I was on vacation all the time. All the costs are approximative

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries are less expensive than DK and transportation is very cheap. Get a leap card

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many clubs and societies. I didn’t join any societies but definitely join the clubs! There is also a free gym available through the university

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined the mountaineering and badminton club, and I really recommend them!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Dingle!! The small villages around Cork, Dublin, hiking-trips with mountaineering club.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, a city filled with students and people are easy going

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs and go to some of the socials they are organizing

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Their accent

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are very welcoming and sweet. The pub culture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Start the application process for accommodation early, travel, go to pubs

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy your time!!! Time flies when you're having fun

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many nice people and getting to know a new country

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing friends and family

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
